message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted speed limit, but drivers must drive “at a safe speed.” | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Guidelines | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | TxDOT – Cell‑Phone Use Policy | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑Tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI Enforcement | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right yields to the left.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School‑Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children.
• No passing on either side of a stopped bus. | TxDOT – School‑Bus Safety | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Drivers must signal and check blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, on sidewalks, or in designated no‑parking zones.
• Parking meters and permit zones enforce local rules. | Local city ordinances | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green light = go; yellow light = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | TxDMV – Insurance | | **Special Rules for Commercial Vehicles** | • Commercial drivers must hold a valid CDL.
• Hours‑of‑Service (HOS) regulations apply. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Emergency Vehicle Exemptions** | • Police, fire, ambulance, and other emergency vehicles may exceed speed limits and ignore certain traffic signals when responding to emergencies. | TxDOT – Emergency Vehicle Policy | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary legal source for all traffic laws. 2. **TxDOT Website** – Offers updates, safety campaigns, and downloadable resources. 3. **TxDMV** – For registration, insurance, and driver licensing information. 4. **Local City Ordinances** – May impose additional rules (e.g., parking restrictions, local speed limits). --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – even on “no‑limit” highways, drive at a safe speed. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. - **Keep a safe following distance** – especially on highways where speeds are high. - **Check for school buses** – stop immediately when a bus stops to pick up or drop off children. - **Stay alert for pedestrians** – give them priority at crosswalks. - **Carry proof of insurance** – it’s required by law and can save you trouble in an accident. Feel free to ask if you’d like more detailed information on any specific area (e.g., DUI penalties, school‑bus rules, or commercial driving regulations).
